name: cal_2x11_v5d
notes:
cal_2x11_v5d - 2026-08-13. FINAL, BENCH-CUT AND LOCKED, ALL CELLS MEASURED. The operating profile. Cells 3 and 4 were placed by hand in pimd_delaycal v1.49 Manual Nudge against live target charts, not solved to a voltage target; cell 4 was then trimmed on both bands to close a cross-band mismatch, and that trim is bench-confirmed - see CELL 4 RE-CUT below. Every voltage in the table below is measured. NEXT STEP: BUILD THE CORPUS against this profile.

LINEAGE. cal_2x11_v5a -> v5b (top anchor 2.4 V -> 4.7 V, ladder re-cut, bench-locked) -> v5c -> v5d. Against v5b, only cells 3 and 4 moved, both earlier on both bands:
  100 us band  cell 3  12.704 -> 12.136 (-568 ns)   cell 4  13.872 -> 13.248 (-624 ns)   cell 5  15.064 -> 15.088 (+24 ns)
   10 us band  cell 2   8.384 ->  8.376 (  -8 ns)   cell 3   9.648 ->  9.088 (-560 ns)   cell 4  10.776 -> 10.176 (-600 ns)
Cells 1, 2 and 6-11 are unchanged from v5b, which carried 6-11 unchanged from v5a. Geometry, band frequencies, pulse widths and averages are unchanged throughout.

WHY CELLS 3 AND 4 MOVED EARLIER. On v5b the steepest part of the measured target response sat in the cell 2 -> cell 3 gap, and cell 3 was placed past the knee, so the response curve read as a kink rather than a shape. Moving both cells earlier puts them on that limb. The gaps are 1.936 / 0.744 / 1.112 / 1.840 us on the 100 us band and 1.880 / 0.712 / 1.088 / 1.784 us on the 10 us - deliberately uneven, tight through the knee and wide either side, which is the opposite of v5b's even-in-log-amplitude ladder and is the point of the change.

MEASURED IN AIR at steady state, 1 666 sweeps over 93 s, zero flagged rows, pack 20.17 V, board 49.4 C (session_20260813_200336, fw v4.37, classviz v1.79, recorded against the re-cut geometry):
  cell  thr      100 us delay / mean     10 us delay / mean     cross-band
   1   4.700 V    9.456 us  4680.0 mV     6.496 us  4696.0 mV     0.34 %
   2   1.900 V   11.392 us  1874.3 mV     8.376 us  1898.5 mV     1.28 %
   3   1.150 V   12.136 us  1133.2 mV     9.088 us  1151.0 mV     1.56 %
   4   0.500 V   13.248 us   498.9 mV    10.176 us   499.4 mV     0.09 %  <- tightest anchor, see CELL 4 RE-CUT
   5   0.125 V   15.088 us   123.0 mV    11.960 us   124.2 mV     0.91 %
   6     ord     15.872 us    79.0 mV    12.896 us    77.9 mV     1.32 %
   7     ord     16.920 us    62.5 mV    13.800 us    69.9 mV    11.32 %  (null minimum, band-dependent by construction)
   8     ord     21.160 us    91.8 mV    16.160 us    92.0 mV     0.24 %
   9     ord     37.736 us   111.8 mV    19.640 us   108.0 mV     3.45 %
  10     ord     67.296 us   112.3 mV    23.864 us   109.9 mV     2.15 %
  11     ord    120.000 us   112.0 mV    29.000 us   111.0 mV     0.93 %
Air std dev 0.07-0.88 mV per cell on the 100 us band and 0.05-0.23 mV on the 10 us. Sweep rate 17.86 Hz, unchanged from v5a/v5b as expected - the geometry did not change.

CELL 4 RE-CUT - BENCH-CONFIRMED. As hand-placed at 13.272 / 10.160 us, cell 4 read 491.4 mV on the 100 us band against 507.2 mV on the 10 us - a 3.16 % cross-band mismatch, against 0.26 % on v5b, because the hand placement moved the two bands by slightly different amounts on a steep part of the decay. Cells 1-5 are meant to be amplitude-matched across bands so that cell index n is the same point on the decay in either band. It was closed by trimming both bands onto the 500 mV consensus - 100 us 13.272 -> 13.248 us (-24 ns), 10 us 10.160 -> 10.176 us (+16 ns) - with step sizes taken from the measured local log-slopes either side of cell 4, 0.73837 (cells 3-4) and 0.78010 (cells 4-5) nepers/us. Predicted 500.1 / 500.9 mV at 0.15 %; MEASURED 498.9 / 499.4 mV at 0.09 %, i.e. -1.2 / -1.5 mV against prediction (-0.24 % / -0.30 %, both low, consistent with the pack having fallen from 20.70 to 20.17 V between the two measurements) and better cross-band than predicted. Cell 4 is now the tightest-matched anchor in the profile.

PACK SENSITIVITY, TWO MEASUREMENTS. The same cells at pack 20.70 V / board 49.0 C (session_20260813_193503) read 4685.8 / 4698.4 mV on cell 1 against 4680.0 / 4696.0 mV at 20.17 V / 49.4 C above. Both cuts are near the BOTTOM of the DESIGN section 12 clean window. That pair gives cell 1 a supply sensitivity of 10.9 mV/V on the 100 us band and 4.5 mV/V on the 10 us - see DESIGN fact 17.23 and its 2026-08-13 qualifier, which is the reference for this, NOT section 12. (Earlier versions of these notes carried a figure of 43-51 mV/V citing section 12; DESIGN does not support it and never did - 17.23 puts the GRID MEAN at ~1 mV/V, with individual steep cells departing from that by an order of magnitude. The 43-51 figure was inherited from cal_2x11_v5a's notes and is withdrawn.) Extrapolating 10.9 mV/V from 20.17 V to a full 24 V pack puts cell 1 near 4.72 V against the 5.000 V ADC full scale - comfortable, and roughly 130 mV more headroom than the withdrawn figure implied. Treat that as indicative only: it extrapolates 3.8 V from a 0.53 V measured span, across which board temperature also moved 49.0 -> 49.4 C. Cell 1 still wants checking on a genuinely full pack rather than trusted from this; if it ever clips, the top anchor has to come down and the ladder be re-cut.

EARLY DELAY. Cell 1 sits at 6.496 / 9.456 us, earlier than anything used before v5b and earlier than the ~9-12 us window the scope captures cover, so the front-end transient is not independently characterised there. It measures clean - 0.23 / 0.80 mV air std dev, 0.34 % cross-band agreement.

VALIDATED OFFLINE against the firmware's own compute_pulse_duties / pulse_duties_valid: every delay an exact multiple of the 8 ns PWM grid, every (drive_duty, sample_duty) pair inside 16 bits with sample strictly after drive, delays strictly increasing and threshold_v strictly descending. The 10 us band's last cell keeps 96 ns of margin (157 counts).

threshold_v - MIXED MEANING. Cells 1-5 carry REAL measured amplitudes in volts: 4.700 / 1.900 / 1.150 / 0.500 / 0.125. These are what pimd_delaycal keys its nudge targets on, and they are pack-state dependent as described. Cells 6-11 are time-anchored and band-dependent, so their entries are PLACEHOLDER ORDERING KEYS ONLY - 100 / 90 / 80 / 70 / 60 / 50 mV, chosen only to keep the column strictly descending (marked 'ord' in the table). Do not mine cells 6-11 as voltages; the null minimum measures 62.5 / 69.9 mV, not 90.

GEOMETRY PIN. Any edit to this file - including this notes text - changes profile_sha8 and therefore the (profile_name, profile_sha8) comparability guard in pimd_features. Frames recorded under a different sha8 must never be mixed with corpus rows recorded under this one (DESIGN section 10). RELOAD THE PROFILE IN THE TOOL BEFORE RECORDING, so the corpus is stamped against this file. This file has carried three sha8s, all before any corpus existed: 48de8676 (cell 4 hand-placed, nothing recorded against it), 6339c35e (cell 4 re-cut, notes carrying the predicted values - the two air validation sessions 195332 and 200336 are stamped with this one), and the current hash after those predictions were replaced with the measured values above. The delays and threshold_v have not changed since 6339c35e - only this notes text - so the two air sessions remain physically comparable to anything recorded now, but the guard will not know that and will group them separately.

Session provenance: no sweep - delays imported from cal_2x11_v5c and hand-edited. Saved 2026-08-13 19:34:44, delaycal v1.49, averages N=32, signal detect 5.0 V, std dev N=8. Conditions at save: pack 21.40 -> 20.82 V, board 47.3 -> 47.2 C. Note that delaycal and classviz are not at the same thermal state at handover - classviz is the authority for these voltages; see the 2026-08-13 findings entry in CHANGELOG.md.
